header.running_head: 2. The Effects of the Qur'an and Hadith...

blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Ibn Abbas (RA) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said, “Be careful in hearing Hadith from me and narrating it to others; narrate only those Ahadith which you clearly know to be Hadith. Whoever, knowing it to be wrong, says that what I did not say is my Hadith, let him make his abode in the Fire! One who explains the Qur'an according to his own opinion, let him make his abode in the Fire.”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ جُنْدُبٍ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ: مَنْ قَالَ فِي كِتَابِ اللهِ بِرَأْيِهِ فَأَصَابَ فَقَدْ أَخْطَأَ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه ابوداؤد باب الكلام في كتاب الله بلا علم رقم:٣٦٥٢
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Jundub (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said, “Whoever, when explaining the Qur'an, says something according to his own opinion, even if it is in fact correct, he has made a mistake.”

blocks.text:
Explanation:- A person gives an explanation of the Qur'an using his own intellect and opinion. Even though that explanation happens by chance to be correct, he has made a mistake, because for this commentary (Tafsir) he did not turn to the Ahadith, nor did he turn to the Ulama of the Ummah.
(Mazahir-e-Haq)
2. The Effects of the Qur'an and Hadith

blocks.arabic_text: قَالَ اللهُ تَعَالي: (وَإِذَا سَمِعُوا مَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَي الرَّسُولِ تَرَي أَعْيُنَهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ مِمَّا عَرَفُوا مِنَ الْحَقِّ۞).
